newsitem.title: UK: HEALTH - Workplaces can cause asthma, experts warn.
newsitem.headline: HEALTH - Workplaces can cause asthma, experts warn.

text.p: As many as one in five cases of asthma could be caused by chemicals and other substances at work, experts said on Friday.

More than 200 different agents ranging from coffee grains to henna can cause the allergic reaction that marks asthma, Dr Katherine Venables of London's National Heart and Lung Institute and Moira Chang-Yeung of the University of British Columbia said.
Any time an adult comes down with asthma the possibility of workplace exposure should be considered, they said in a report for the Lancet medical journal.
The symptoms of asthma range from a mild sneeze or cough to severe shortness of breath.
"Occupational asthma is a potentially fatal condition," Venables and Chang-Yeung warned.
If occupational asthma is diagnosed, the worker should get away from whatever is causing it, be it woodchips, latex or metal dust.
"Patients who remain in the same job and continue to be exposed to the same causal agent after diagnosis worsen with time."
Between five and 10 percent of the population suffers from asthma.
